children.text: Most note apps don't handle real-time multi-user editing well. I wanted to understand how operational transforms and conflict resolution actually work under the hood instead of just using a library blindly.

I chose Redis pub/sub over a plain in-memory broadcast because the app needed to support horizontal scaling across multiple Node instances - in-memory state would break the moment there is more than one server process.

name: Redis
reason: Pub/sub across multiple Node instances, so state survives horizontal scaling

children.text: Handling out-of-order WebSocket messages during reconnects was the hardest part. Solved it with a sequence-numbered event log per document.
Without sequence numbers, a reconnecting client could replay stale edits and silently overwrite newer ones.
Sub-200ms sync latency between clients in testing, supports 10+ concurrent editors per document.
